fields.description: The seller SKU this enrichment is for — also the name of its Amazon Product Listing. Plain Data rather than a Link so this app stays installable without the Amazon connector.
fields.label: SKU

fields.description: Mirrors the listing's `title`. Amazon truncates past 200 characters.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: Amazon's product type for this listing, e.g. TOWEL. Every update Amazon accepts has to declare one, so a listing without it cannot be published to at all. Classified from the ENRICHED title on every run, so it can differ from what the listing sells as today — where it does, Needs Review says so. Approval writes this value onto the Amazon Product Listing, so correct it before approving if it is wrong.
fields.label: Product Type

fields.description: Amazon's own display name for the product type, when it gave one. A label only — `product_type` is the value that gets published.
fields.label: Product Type (Display Name)

fields.description: Where the product type came from. `suggested` is Amazon's best match for the ENRICHED title — the normal answer, and one worth confirming. `listing` means Amazon had nothing to say about the new title, so the type this listing already published with was kept. `reviewer` means a human typed or picked this one, which outranks both. `none` means nobody has picked one yet.
fields.label: Product Type Source

fields.description: Which of this site's own house brands this listing's product belongs to, classified by the agent from the finished title and description -- never from its category (Item Group), which is a fact about where the product sells today, not about which of this site's own brands it belongs to. Empty means either this site has no house brands at all, or the agent didn't think any of them fit; both leave the choice to a reviewer. Lives on this enrichment record only -- never written to the Amazon Product Listing.
fields.label: Brand

fields.description: The listing's key product features, in order. Amazon accepts at most five — these are what approval publishes, so edit them here before approving.
fields.label: Bullet Points

fields.description: Plain text, no HTML or markdown. Amazon truncates past 2000 characters.
fields.label: Description

fields.description: Amazon BACKEND search terms — never shown to a shopper. These become the listing's `keywords` on approval, so edit them here before approving. Amazon indexes roughly the first 250 bytes and ignores the rest.
fields.label: Keywords

fields.description: Images are produced after the listing text is saved, so a listing can be ready to review while its imagery is still rendering.
fields.label: Image Status
fields.options:
Not Required
Queued
Running
Ready
Partial
Failed

fields.description: Tokens the image service billed for this listing. Recorded here rather than on the run, because the imagery is produced after the run closes.
fields.label: Image Tokens

fields.description: Thumbnails of what the image step produced; the child table below is always the editable source.
fields.label: Image Preview

fields.description: Images this run produced. Source photos are never overwritten. On approval the rows that have a URL replace the listing's image set, the first of them as the main image.
fields.label: Images

fields.description: Fields the agent could not confidently fill — complete these before approving.
fields.label: Needs Review

fields.description: Assumptions the agent made, which of Amazon's own listing issues this enrichment addresses, and which the admin still has to handle.
fields.label: Notes

fields.description: The bullet points exactly as the agent returned them, kept for audit. The Bullet Points table is what gets published — editing this changes nothing.
fields.label: Bullet Points (JSON)

fields.description: The keywords exactly as the agent returned them, kept for audit. The Keywords table is what gets published — editing this changes nothing.
fields.label: Keywords (JSON)

fields.description: Amazon's candidate product types for this listing, best match first, as [{product_type, display_name}]. Looked up from the ENRICHED title above rather than the raw one — a product type has to describe the copy that will actually be published. The Product Type field offers these as options; this is the record of what Amazon said on the day it was asked.
fields.label: Product Type Suggestions (JSON)

fields.description: Verbatim JSON returned by the agent, kept for audit.
fields.label: Raw Agent Output (JSON)
